exact_repo_excerpts.lem-smc-multinomial-variance-unrolls:
Use the operators and multinomial variance recursion of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]] at every selection time. For $\phi\in\Psi_t^{(d)}$, put $\bar\phi=\phi-\pi_t(\phi)$. Then
$$V_t(\phi)=\sum_{k=0}^{t}\widetilde\pi_k\!\left[\upsilon_k^2\,E_{k+1:t}(\bar\phi)E_{k+1:t}(\bar\phi)^\top\right],$$
where the $k=t$ term uses $E_{t+1:t}\bar\phi=\bar\phi$. Each summand is a finite positive-semidefinite matrix under the stated class conditions.
exact_repo_excerpts.lem-smc-backward-operator-oscillation-bo:
Let $E_s$ be the forward operators of [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]], and for bounded real $h$ put $\operatorname{osc}(h)=\sup h-\inf h$. Suppose there is one $\beta\in[0,1)$ such that
$$\operatorname{osc}(E_s h)\le\beta\operatorname{osc}(h)$$
for every $s$ and every bounded real $h$. For bounded $\phi:\Theta_t\to\mathbb R$, put $\Delta\phi=\operatorname{osc}(\phi)$ and $\bar\phi=\phi-\pi_t(\phi)$. Then for every $0\le k\le t$,
$$\bigl\lVert E_{k+1:t}\bar\phi\bigr\rVert_\infty\le\beta^{t-k}\Delta\phi,$$
with $\beta^0=1$ and $E_{t+1:t}$ the identity. This condition concerns the actual SMC backward operators; it is not implied merely by mixing ratios of the proposal densities.
exact_repo_excerpts.lem-dobrushin-contraction-from-density-r:
Let $K:S\rightsquigarrow E$ be a probability kernel on a nonempty measurable source space. Suppose a sigma-finite measure $\lambda$ on $E$ and probability densities $k_x$ satisfy $K(x,A)=\int_A k_x\,d\lambda$ for every $x\in S$ and measurable $A\subseteq E$. If $C\ge1$ and, for every $x,x'\in S$, $k_x(z)\le Ck_{x'}(z)$ for $\lambda$-almost every $z$, then the Dobrushin coefficient from [[def-dobrushin-coefficient-for-probability-kernels]] obeys
$$\delta(K)\le1-C^{-1}.$$
exact_repo_excerpts.def-dobrushin-coefficient-for-probabilit:
Let $(S,\Sigma)$ and $(E,\mathcal E)$ be measurable spaces with $S\ne\varnothing$, and let $K:S\rightsquigarrow E$ be a probability kernel as in [[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]. Its **Dobrushin contraction coefficient** is
$$\delta(K):=\sup_{x,x'\in S}\lVert K(x,\cdot)-K(x',\cdot)\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}},$$
where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}$ is the event-supremum distance between probability laws in [[def-total-variation-distance-for-probability-laws]]. Thus $0\le\delta(K)\le1$. The coefficient measures the largest total-variation separation between two one-step output laws.
exact_repo_excerpts.thm-smc-time-uniform-variance-bound-unde:
Use multinomial offspring resampling at every time and the variance $V_t$ in [[def-smc-clt-function-classes-and-variance-recursions]]. Assume there is a constant $B<\infty$ such that $\upsilon_s\le B$ $\widetilde\pi_s$-almost everywhere for every $s\ge0$. Assume also that the forward operators satisfy the uniform oscillation condition of [[lem-smc-backward-operator-oscillation-bound]] with one $\beta\in[0,1)$ for all times. Then every bounded real test $\phi$ with $\Delta\phi=\sup\phi-\inf\phi<\infty$ satisfies
$$V_t(\phi)\le\frac{B^2(\Delta\phi)^2}{1-\beta^2}\qquad(t\ge0).$$
This is a bound on the fixed-horizon CLT variance, uniform in the time index; it is not a finite-particle error bound.
exact_repo_excerpts.cex-smc-time-bound-fails-with-varying-pr:
refuted

Uniform bounds on the true transition density ratios $g(x\mid x')/g(x\mid x'')$ and proposal density ratios $q_t(x\mid x')/q_t(x\mid x'')$, together with a likelihood bounded above and away from zero and a bounded test oscillation, suffice by themselves to keep the SIR asymptotic variance $V_t(\phi)$ bounded uniformly in time.

proposed_supplier.status: complete mathematical proposal in research only; not an authored carrier or native review
proposed_supplier.statement: Let (X,E) be a nonempty standard-Borel measurable space with sigma-finite measure lambda. Fix a probability eta_0. For each s>=1 let g_s(z|x) be a jointly measurable, strictly positive finite density of a probability transition with respect to lambda. Suppose a constant C>=1 satisfies g_s(z|x)<=C g_s(z|x') for every s and all x,x',z. (The time-homogeneous case g_s=g is included.) Let f_s be measurable with 0<a<=f_s(z)<=b<infinity uniformly. Define eta_s(h)=eta_{s-1}(g_s(f_s h))/eta_{s-1}(g_s f_s) and c_s=eta_{s-1}(g_s f_s). Define E_s h(x)=g_s(f_s h)(x)/c_s, acting on last-state functions. These are exactly the SIR path operators restricted to last-state functions whenever the proposal q_s has appropriate support and its normalized incremental weight is g_s(z|x)f_s(z)/(c_s q_s(z|x)). Let rho=1-C^(-2). For every bounded measurable real terminal test psi and 0<=k<t, ||E_{k+1}...E_t(psi-eta_t psi)||_infinity<=C rho^(t-k) osc(psi). For k=t the identity image is bounded by osc(psi). Here rho^n=0 for n>=1 when C=1. This is a filtering-test statement, not a statement about arbitrary path observables.
proposed_supplier.proof:
1. For fixed k<t define Q_{k,t}h(x)=integral [product_{j=k+1}^t g_j(x_j|x_{j-1})f_j(x_j)]h(x_t) d lambda^{t-k}, with x_k=x, and H_{j,t}=Q_{j,t}1, H_{t,t}=1. Kernel iteration defines these integrals without choosing product-density versions. They are measurable and a^(t-j)<=H_{j,t}<=b^(t-j), since each g_j is a probability density. They are therefore positive and finite. Comparing the first transition density in H_{j,t}(x) and H_{j,t}(x') gives H_{j,t}(x)<=C H_{j,t}(x') whenever j<t. Consequently r_{k,t}=H_{k,t}/eta_k(H_{k,t})<=C and eta_k r_{k,t}=1.
2. For j=k+1,...,t set L_{j,t}(x,dz)=g_j(z|x)f_j(z)H_{j,t}(z)lambda(dz)/H_{j-1,t}(x). These are measurable probability kernels by the backward recursion for H. Their ordered density ratios equal [g_j(z|x)/g_j(z|x')][H_{j-1,t}(x')/H_{j-1,t}(x)]<=C^2. The established normalized-density-ratio lemma yields delta(L_{j,t})<=1-C^(-2)=rho.
3. For a probability kernel K and a bounded measurable h with osc(h)>0, set u=(h-inf h)/osc(h), so 0<=u<=1. For any x,x', the layer-cake identity K u(x)-K u(x')=integral_0^1 [K(x,{u>r})-K(x',{u>r})]dr yields |K h(x)-K h(x')|<=delta(K)osc(h). If osc(h)=0 the same conclusion follows because K preserves constants. Taking suprema gives osc(Kh)<=delta(K)osc(h). Iterating over the L kernels gives osc(P_{k,t}h)<=rho^(t-k)osc(h), where P_{k,t}=L_{k+1,t}...L_{t,t}. Telescoping their H denominators proves P_{k,t}h=Q_{k,t}h/H_{k,t}.
4. The recursion for eta gives eta_t h=eta_k(Q_{k,t}h)/eta_k(H_{k,t}) and product_{j=k+1}^t c_j=eta_k(H_{k,t}). Therefore E_{k+1}...E_t h=r_{k,t}P_{k,t}h. Put h=psi-eta_t psi. Then eta_k(r_{k,t}P_{k,t}h)=0. Since r_{k,t}eta_k is a probability measure, inf(P_{k,t}h)<=0<=sup(P_{k,t}h), including the case it vanishes almost everywhere. Hence ||P_{k,t}h||_infinity<=osc(P_{k,t}h)<=rho^(t-k)osc(psi). Multiplying by 0<r_{k,t}<=C proves the estimate. At k=t, eta_t psi lies between inf psi and sup psi, giving the identity-case estimate. No positivity assumption about h is used.
proposed_supplier.variance_corollary_statement: In addition to the preceding filtering hypotheses, take measurable strictly positive finite proposal densities q_s and a uniform domination g_s(z|x)<=D q_s(z|x), with D<infinity. Suppose the initial normalized incremental Radon-Nikodym weight satisfies v_0<=B_init almost everywhere under its proposal. Use multinomial selection at every time. Set B=max(B_init,D b/a). For every bounded last-state test psi, the weighted-estimator fixed-horizon CLT asymptotic variance is bounded, uniformly over t, by B^2 C^2 osc(psi)^2/[1-(1-C^(-2))^2]. No claim about finite-particle errors or arbitrary path tests is made.
proposed_supplier.variance_corollary_proof: The denominator c_s=eta_{s-1}(g_s f_s) lies in [a,b], so the normalized incremental weight v_s(x,z)=g_s(z|x)f_s(z)/(c_s q_s(z|x)) satisfies v_s<=Db/a for every s>=1. Together with the initial bound this gives v_s<=B at every time. Bounded filtering tests and the finite-horizon bounded E-images in the supplier meet the recursive moment-class requirements. Apply the multinomial unrolling formula to h=psi-eta_t psi. The final k=t contribution is at most B^2 osc(psi)^2. The k<t contribution is at most B^2 C^2 rho^(2(t-k))osc(psi)^2 by the supplier. Thus V_t(psi)<=B^2 osc(psi)^2[1+C^2 sum_{n=1}^t rho^(2n)]<=B^2 C^2 osc(psi)^2/(1-rho^2). When C=1, all earlier contributions vanish and the same formula holds. For each finite horizon the probability weights and bounded images make all required moments finite. The optional sharper B constant follows from v_s^2<=B v_s and proposal(v_s)=1, but is unnecessary.
proposed_supplier.scope_note: All-parent/all-z strictly positive finite density versions stated above avoid joint exceptional-set/version issues in this proposed carrier. These are explicit sufficient hypotheses; this branch makes no assertion that arbitrary almost-everywhere row-ratio versions automatically provide all-parent versions.
